meta.title: ly to mi Converter — Light Year to Mile
meta.description: Convert Light Year (ly) to Mile (mi) instantly. 1 ly = 5.878606e+12 mi. Free, accurate, browser-based.

content.intro: Convert light years (ly) to miles (mi) instantly. Both measure length, so the relationship is strictly linear: each light year equals 5.878606e+12 miles. Use the converter above for any value, or read on for the formula, a quick lookup table, and practical tips.
content.result_section: One light year is equal to **5.878606e+12 miles**. To go the other way, one mile equals **1.701083e-13 light years**. For everyday use, rounding to 2–4 decimal places is usually enough; for engineering or scientific work, keep the full precision shown by the converter.
content.formula_section:
The conversion is a single multiplication:

> miles = light years × 5.878606e+12

Worked example — converting 10 light years:

10 × 5.878606e+12 = **5.878606e+13 mi**.

To invert, divide by 5.878606e+12 (or multiply by 1.701083e-13).

- Travel planning where signage and maps use different unit systems.
- DIY and home-improvement projects that mix metric materials with imperial tools.
- Fitness tracking when devices report in one system and goals are set in another.
- Shipping and logistics where weight and dimensions drive cost.
content.tips:
Keep the factor handy: 1 ly ≈ 5.878606e+12 mi. For rough mental math, round to the nearest sensible digit.

Mind the units. Light Year and Mile both measure length; squared or cubic variants need a different factor (factor², factor³).

When precision matters (engineering, lab work, dosing), avoid rounding mid-calculation — convert once at the final step using the full factor.
content.faq:
**Q:** How many miles are in 1 light year?
**A:** 5.878606e+12 miles.

**Q:** What's the formula to convert ly to mi?
**A:** miles = light years × 5.878606e+12.

**Q:** How do I convert mi back to ly?
**A:** Multiply by 1.701083e-13 (or divide by 5.878606e+12).

**Q:** Is rounding to 2 decimal places accurate enough?
**A:** For most everyday uses, yes. For scientific or engineering work, use the full precision from the converter.

**Q:** Does this ly to mi converter work offline?
**A:** Yes — all math runs in your browser, no network required after the page loads.
